column9: note
Boehm 1871 (Miller 1922 p.14): main part cylindrical, inside diameter 19 mm; JSV 2001 states the same 19 mm
Miller 1922 p.54 bracket: silver tubes used by Boehm about 0.28 mm thick (a later passage on flute making rounds to about 0.3 mm)
Miller 1922 p.36 bracket: open end of a B foot-joint 663.62 mm from the cork face (C-foot end 623.50 mm)
DERIVED, not measured: x' = (x + 0.0515)*(435/440) - 0.0515 m, the Schema pitch rule of Miller 1922 pp.41-44 (theoretical length scales with 1/pitch, the 51.5 mm closed-end term is subtracted again)
Miller 1922 p.17 Fig.8: tapered portion of an excellent Boehm and Mendler head-joint is 134 mm long, measured from the cork
Miller 1922 p.17 Fig.8: bore diameter 17.1 mm at the cork; intermediate diameters are on the figure only (u-taper-profile)
Miller 1922 p.17 Fig.8: diameters rise by 0.1 mm per section up to 19.0 mm near the tuning slide
Boehm 1871 (Miller 1922 p.14): bore of the head-joint reduced by two millimetres from the joint upwards to the cork
Boehm 1871 (Miller 1922 p.20): stopper position found to be 17 mm from the centre of the embouchure
Wolfe et al. 2001 JSV Methods: cork set 17.5 mm from the centre of the embouchure hole for the standard measurements (Pearl PF-661); +-0.5 mm is an assumed bound, not stated
Wolfe et al. 2001 JSV Methods: tuning slide set at 4 mm for the standard measurements (Pearl PF-661)
Boehm 1871 (Miller 1922 p.24): mouth-hole 10 mm wide and 12 mm long is best suited to most players
Boehm 1871 (Miller 1922 p.24): 12 mm long; Miller measured many Boehm and Mendler flutes: average 10.4 mm by 12.2 mm
Boehm 1871 (Miller 1922 p.23): angle of 7 degrees between the hole sides and the section through the air column axis
Boehm 1871 (Miller 1922 p.23-24): walls of the mouth-hole 4.2 mm thick (height of the sides)
Wolfe, Smith and Green 2003 WESPAC Fig.2 caption: measured embouchure riser length 5 mm (Pearl PF-661)
Wolfe, Smith and Green 2003 WESPAC Fig.2 caption: truncated flanged cone, radius 5.8 mm outside
Wolfe, Smith and Green 2003 WESPAC Fig.2 caption: radius 6.4 mm inside the instrument
Wolfe et al. 2001 JSV Methods: area of the embouchure hole (about 90 mm2); about is the source's word
